routes.label: Use the sum 10 and reject repeated digits
Express every circle using the top digit

question:
In the figure below, each circle will be filled with a digit from \(1\) to \(6.\) Each digit must appear exactly once. The sum of the digits in neighboring circles is shown in the box between them. What digit must be placed in the top circle?

[Figure 1](figures/2026_AMC_8_Q12_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Start with the largest neighboring sum, \(10\), because there are very few ways to make it using the allowed digits.

[Figure 1](figures/2026_AMC_8_Q12_question_fig1.svg)

The two circles next to the box labeled \(10\) must contain \(4\) and \(6\). The other possibility, \(5+5\), repeats a digit, and any digit smaller than \(4\) would require a partner greater than \(6\).

Suppose the middle circle on the left contained \(6\). Then the bottom-left circle would contain \(10-6=4\), and the bottom-middle circle would contain \(8-4=4\). This repeats \(4\), so this placement is impossible.

Therefore the middle circle on the left contains \(4\), making the top digit
\[
9-4=5.
\]
A complete filling, read clockwise from the top, is \(5,1,3,2,6,4\). These use each digit exactly once and give successive neighboring sums \(6,4,5,8,10,9\), matching all six boxes. Thus the required digit is \(5\), choice D.
